title: OFFSET FETCH
description: Learn how to use the OFFSET FETCH clauses to limit the number of rows returned by a query, ideal for implementing paging solutions.

data.alt: SQL Server OFFSET FETCH skip 10 rows fetch next 10 rows example
SQL Server OFFSET FETCH result set

data.text: The OFFSET and FETCH clauses are optional clauses of the ORDER BY clause. They allow you to limit the number of rows returned by a query, making them ideal for implementing paging solutions.

data.title: OFFSET FETCH Syntax
data.content: OFFSET specifies rows to skip, FETCH specifies rows to return.

items: The OFFSET clause specifies the number of rows to skip before starting to return rows from the query. The offset_row_count can be a constant, variable, or parameter that is greater than or equal to zero.
The FETCH clause specifies the number of rows to return after the OFFSET clause has been processed. The fetch_row_count can be a constant, variable, or scalar that is greater than or equal to one.
The OFFSET clause is mandatory, while the FETCH clause is optional.
FIRST and NEXT are synonyms and can be used interchangeably. Similarly, ROW and ROWS can be used interchangeably.

data.title: Important
data.text: You must use the OFFSET and FETCH clauses with the ORDER BY clause. Otherwise, you will encounter an error.

data.title: OFFSET FETCH vs TOP
data.text: The OFFSET and FETCH clauses are preferable for implementing paging solutions compared to the TOP clause.

data.title: Version Support
data.text: The OFFSET and FETCH clauses have been available since SQL Server 2012 (11.x) and later, as well as Azure SQL Database.

data.title: Skip First 10 Rows
data.content: Skip the first 10 rows and return the rest.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
ORDER BY
    list_price,
    product_name
OFFSET 10 ROWS;

data.title: Skip 10, Fetch Next 10
data.content: Skip the first 10 rows and return the next 10 rows for paging.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
ORDER BY
    list_price,
    product_name
OFFSET 10 ROWS
FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY;

data.title: Top 10 Most Expensive Products
data.content: Use OFFSET 0 to start from the first row and FETCH FIRST 10 to get 10 rows.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
ORDER BY
    list_price DESC,
    product_name
OFFSET 0 ROWS
FETCH FIRST 10 ROWS ONLY;

data.text: In this example, the ORDER BY clause sorts the products by their list prices in descending order. Then, the OFFSET clause skips zero rows, and the FETCH clause retrieves the first 10 products from the list.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use OFFSET to skip a specified number of rows before returning rows.
Use FETCH to specify how many rows to return after the OFFSET.
OFFSET is mandatory; FETCH is optional but commonly used for paging.
OFFSET FETCH must always be used with ORDER BY.
OFFSET FETCH is preferred over TOP for implementing paging solutions.
